# Does Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) Have an API? Every Route, Compared (November 2026)

**Short answer (November 8, 2026).** Partly. Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) now has a developer API, the Gemini Notebook API: a Public Preview for personal Google accounts, at no charge during the preview. It only creates notebooks and adds sources: it generates no content of any kind (no audio or video overviews, reports, mind maps, quizzes or slide decks) and cannot answer questions about your sources. The Enterprise API makes only audio overviews, for licensed users at $9 per license per month (minimum 15). The Podcast API is deprecated. Unofficial libraries and hosted services use your own account, at your risk; AutoContent API is an independent alternative.

How we checked. We ran AutoContent API ourselves on November 2, 2026, checked Google's pages again on November 3, and added Google's new Gemini Notebook API from its documentation on November 8. Every other route is described from its own documentation, with the date of that documentation. Originally published November 23, 2024.

## Every route, compared

| Route | What it makes | Access and price | Terms risk | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gemini Notebook API (Google, Public Preview) | Nothing generated: it only creates, lists and updates notebooks, and adds web pages, YouTube videos, plain text and Markdown as sources. The API has no method for audio or video overviews, reports, mind maps, quizzes, infographics, slide decks or questions. A remote MCP server gives the same notebook and source tools. | No charge during the Public Preview. A personal Google account (Workspace accounts are not supported yet), a Google Cloud project and an OAuth 2.0 user token; the API takes no API keys. 100 requests per minute per project; 100 to 500 notebooks per user, by Google plan. | Low, with Preview terms. Google's own API in your Google Cloud project. Google can change or stop a Preview at any time, with no SLA. | From its docs, updated October 29 to November 2, 2026. Not run by us. |
| Gemini Notebook Enterprise API (Google) | Notebooks, sources and audio overviews, one per notebook at a time. The API has no video overview, slide deck or infographic, and no method to download the audio. | A Google Cloud project and a signed-in user with a Gemini Notebook Enterprise license. $9 per license per month, at least 15 licenses. 20 audio overviews per user per day. | Low, with Preview terms. Google's own API under your Google Cloud agreement. Google can change or stop a Preview at any time, with no SLA. | From its docs, updated October 28 to November 5, 2026. Not run by us. |
| Podcast API (Google) | A podcast from text or media that you send, with no notebook: `SHORT` (typically 4 to 5 minutes) or `STANDARD` (around 10 minutes), as MP3. | Deprecated. Google adds no new customers to its allowlist. | Not open to new customers. | From its docs, November 7, 2026. |
| Gemini API text-to-speech (Google), with your own script | Audio from a script that you write, with up to 2 speakers. It does not read sources or make video, slides or infographics. | Self-serve API key. $0.135 per 10 minutes of audio (gemini-3.8-flash-tts, standard tier), $0.27 from January 1, 2027. One call returns at most about 11 minutes of audio. | Low. Google's paid API terms. | From its docs, read November 2, 2026 (the pages show no date). |
| notebooklm-py (open source) | Every Studio output: audio and video overviews, slide decks, infographics, quizzes, mind maps and more, from Python, a CLI or an MCP server. | Free software (MIT) that you run. It signs in with cookies from your own Google account. | High. It uses undocumented Google endpoints on a consumer account. Its README: “Unofficial Library - Use at Your Own Risk”. | From its docs, v0.8.6, October 29, 2026. |
| gemini-notebook-mcp-cli (open source; formerly notebooklm-mcp-cli) | A CLI and an MCP server with 53 tools: audio and video overviews, slide decks, infographics, quizzes, reports and more. | Free software (MIT) that you run. It signs in with cookies from your own Google account, which last about 2 to 4 weeks. | High. Its README says that the internal APIs it uses “may not be aligned with Google's Terms of Service”. | From its docs, v0.15.9, November 2, 2026. |
| Hosted APIs on your own Google account (for example useapi.net) | Every Studio output through a hosted REST API and an MCP server. | useapi.net: $15 per month for up to 3 Google accounts. You add your own Google accounts. | High. Its legal page puts the risk of account bans and suspensions on the user. | From its docs, October 20, 2026 (legal page: October 2026). |
| Composio NotebookLM toolkit | 11 actions for notebooks, sources and audio overviews, for AI agents. | Hosted. It connects by OAuth to NotebookLM Enterprise in your licensed Google Cloud project. Composio plans start at $0 for 100,000 calls per month, plus your Enterprise licenses. | Low, with Preview terms. It acts on the Enterprise product in your own licensed project. | From its docs, toolkit version 20260807_00, read November 2, 2026. |
| ElevenLabs podcast API (not Gemini Notebook) | A one-host or two-host podcast from text or a URL: short (under 3 minutes), default (about 3 to 7) or long (over 7). | The Studio API is available on request through ElevenLabs sales. No price per podcast is published. | Low. ElevenLabs' own API and terms. | From its docs, read November 2, 2026 (the pages show no date). |
| AutoContent API (independent; this site) | Podcasts, explainer videos, slide decks, infographics, quizzes and data tables from URLs, PDFs, YouTube videos and text, with webhooks. | Self-serve API key with a paid plan, from €29 per month: 100 podcasts, €0.29 each. | High. Audio and video overviews, slide decks and infographics are made with Google's Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM), on accounts that AutoContent operates. AutoContent has no agreement with Google. Google can limit or stop this access at any time. | Run by us, November 2, 2026 (test log below). |

Terms risk compares each route with what its provider documents. Low: the route uses an API that its provider documents and sells for this use, under your agreement with that provider. High: the route does not use an API that Google documents for this use, and Google can stop it at any time. This is not a legal opinion. Also found and not in the table: PleasePrompto/notebooklm-mcp (archived in September 2026) and roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp (a self-hosted REST server on your own Google account).

### Which route fits you?

- You only want to create notebooks and add sources from code in your own personal Google account, with nothing generated (no audio, video, report or answers): Google's Gemini Notebook API (Public Preview).
- You need a contract with Google, and audio overviews are enough: the Gemini Notebook Enterprise API.
- You want to automate your own notebooks and you accept the risk: an open-source library or MCP server on your own account.
- You want finished podcasts, videos, slide decks and infographics from one REST call, with no Google account to manage: AutoContent API.
- You want full control of the script and the voices: write the script yourself and use Gemini API text-to-speech.

## The route we ran: AutoContent API on November 2, 2026

We sent six requests with an internal AutoContent token at 20:12 UTC, then ran the code snippets below. The setup is one API key, one create request, then status calls or a webhook: no Google account and no Google Cloud project. Times run from the request to the finished file and include our queue.

| Test | Source (license) | Output | Time to result | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Kubernetes documentation page “Service” (CC BY 4.0) | Podcast, English: 24 min 47 s | 13.2 min | Succeeded |
| 2 | NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0, a 48-page PDF (US government work) | Podcast, English: 22 min 11 s | 9.0 min | Succeeded |
| 3 | NASA video “Our Living Planet From Space”, 5 minutes (public domain) | Podcast, English: 19 min 14 s | 8.6 min | Succeeded |
| 4 | The same NASA video | Podcast, Japanese: 19 min 19 s | 8.6 min | Succeeded |
| 5 | Kubernetes “Service” page | Slide deck: 15 slides (PDF) | 9.9 min | Succeeded |
| 6 | Kubernetes “Service” page | Infographic: one 2752 × 1536 PNG | 2.8 min | Succeeded, with small text errors |
| 7-10 | Kubernetes “Service” page, with the code snippets below | Podcasts, English: 22 min 53 s, 14 min 55 s, 21 min 55 s and 22 min 19 s | 8.5, 7.4, 10.0 and 13.8 min | Succeeded |

What we learned:

- All ten requests succeeded on the first try. The podcasts took 7.4 to 13.8 minutes; our 30-day median for podcasts is 11.5 minutes (see [the developer page](https://autocontentapi.com/developers)).
- With the default length setting, podcasts are long and the length varies: 15 to 25 minutes for the same web page, and 19 minutes from a 5-minute video. The request also takes a `duration` setting (`short`, `default` or `long`).
- The Japanese podcast took the same time as the English one. Whisper detects Japanese, and the first minute, which we checked, is a natural two-host conversation.
- The four podcasts that we measured are at -23 to -25 LUFS. Normalize them to the loudness target of your platform before you publish.
- The slide deck matches the source, including its port examples. The infographic has small text errors, such as a wrong port number and a misspelled domain, so check the text in images before you publish.

![Infographic from test 6: Kubernetes Services, with the four main Service types](https://autocontentapi.com/blog-content/does-notebooklm-have-an-api/kubernetes-service-infographic.webp)

![Slide 14 of 15 from test 5: a decision matrix of the Kubernetes Service types](https://autocontentapi.com/blog-content/does-notebooklm-have-an-api/kubernetes-service-deck-slide-14.webp)

Both outputs are AI-generated with AutoContent API. Audio and video overviews, slide decks and infographics are made with Google's Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM), on accounts that AutoContent operates.

## Google's Enterprise API: documented, not run

We did not run Google's Enterprise API for this update. It needs a Google Cloud project with billing and at least 15 Gemini Notebook Enterprise licenses at $9 per license per month after a trial (Google's product page says 30 days; its licensing docs say 14). This is what Google's documentation of October 28 to November 5, 2026 asks you to do:

1. Start a trial or a subscription, enable the Discovery Engine API, and give each user the Cloud NotebookLM User role and a license.
2. Sign in as that user with `gcloud auth login`. The API needs “an authenticated user account with an active Gemini Notebook Enterprise license”; the docs do not mention service accounts.
3. Create a notebook and add sources: Google Docs or Slides, text, a web page, a YouTube video or an uploaded file.
4. Create the audio overview with an optional `episodeFocus` and `languageCode`. The API has no length setting, and a notebook holds one audio overview at a time.
5. Get the audio: the API has no method to check the status or download the file. The docs say to open the notebook in a browser and download the audio from Studio.

Google's API pages carry a Preview label, but a release note of September 5, 2025 calls notebook creation and management through the API generally available. The audio overview method is Preview.

The call for step 4, adapted from Google's docs (we added a Content-Type header and a closing quote; not run by us):

curl, Gemini Notebook Enterprise API

```
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "https://us-discoveryengine.googleapis.com/v1alpha/projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/us/notebooks/NOTEBOOK_ID/audioOverviews" \
  -d '{"sourceIds": [{"id": "SOURCE_ID"}], "episodeFocus": "EPISODE_FOCUS", "languageCode": "en"}'
```

Google's guide sends these fields at the top level, as above; its REST reference puts them inside `generationOptions`. The answer is `AUDIO_OVERVIEW_STATUS_IN_PROGRESS`, and the docs say it takes a few minutes. Google Cloud documentation is licensed under CC BY 4.0, and its code samples under Apache 2.0.

## What does each route cost you?

Enter your planned podcasts (audio overviews). The calculation runs in your browser.

| Route | Monthly cost at this volume | What else to know |
|---|---|---|
| AutoContent API | Starter: €29 per month (€0.29 per podcast at this volume) | 1,000 credits (10 per podcast, any length); up to 15 per day, depending on credits. Status calls and failed generations use 0 credits. |
| Gemini Notebook Enterprise API | $135.00 per month for 15 licenses | $9 per license per month, at least 15 licenses; 20 audio overviews per licensed user per day. No price per call. Audio overviews only, and you download each one in the browser. |
| Gemini API text-to-speech (you write the script) | $20.25 per month for the audio, $40.50 from January 1, 2027 | 1,500 minutes of audio. Add the model that writes each script, and your own work. |
| Hosted API on your own Google accounts (useapi.net) | $15 per month for up to 3 Google accounts | You add your own Google accounts. Each account's own usage limits apply, and Google can stop the access at any time. |
| Open-source libraries on your own Google account | No price for the software | Your Google account's own usage limits apply, and Google can stop the access at any time. |

AutoContent prices are the monthly EUR plans; the pricing page also shows USD. Google prices are in USD from Google's pages; the sources and dates are in the Sources section.

## Does the API charge for calls?

- **Google's Gemini Notebook API:** no charge during the Public Preview, within its rate limits and the notebook and source limits of your Google plan. The consumer app itself costs nothing with a Google account at standard limits, and Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscriptions raise the limits (Google's plans page).
- **Google's Enterprise API:** its docs show no price per call. You pay for licenses: $9 per license per month, at least 15 licenses, and each licensed user can make 20 audio overviews per day.
- **AutoContent API:** credits per finished output. A podcast uses 10 credits, whatever its length. Status calls and failed generations use 0 credits.
- **Gemini API text-to-speech:** per token, at $9 per million audio tokens on the standard tier: about $0.135 per 10 minutes of audio, plus the model that writes the script. Google's pricing page doubles these prices on January 1, 2027.
- **Open-source tools on your own account:** no price for the software. Your Google account's own usage limits apply.

## What the rename changed for developers

- On July 16, 2026, Google renamed NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook. It is the same standalone product. notebooklm.google.com now redirects to notebook.google.com, and the help center moved to support.google.com/gemininotebook.
- NotebookLM Enterprise became Gemini Notebook Enterprise, and Google says its APIs still use the same endpoints. The technical names did not change: the docs path is still `/notebooklm-enterprise/`, the REST resource is still `projects.locations.notebooks`, the RPC package is still `google.cloud.notebooklm.v1alpha`, the roles are still called Cloud NotebookLM, and the subscription is still named NotebookLM Enterprise.
- Google's fetcher for pages that users add as sources now identifies itself as `Google-GeminiNotebook`. Google supported the former agent, `Google-NotebookLM`, until August 2026. If your firewall or log filters name the old agent, add the new one.
- Google's Enterprise FAQ says that Gemini Notebook Plus for Google Workspace is not a Google Cloud product, and that its notebooks can't be used in Gemini Notebook Enterprise. Workspace Studio flows can add a source to a notebook and ask it questions; they have no audio step.
- notebooklm-py kept its name. notebooklm-mcp-cli moved its repository to gemini-notebook-mcp-cli and kept its package name. When you search for code, use both names.
- Google's new developer API uses only the new name: the Gemini Notebook API, at `notebook.googleapis.com`, documented on developers.google.com/notebook. The Enterprise API keeps its NotebookLM technical names.

## Run it yourself: one podcast from a web page

Each snippet sends the test 1 request without its text instruction, and asks for the result every 30 seconds. Set `AUTOCONTENT_API_KEY` on your server first; never put the key in browser code.

curl, with jq

```
REQUEST_ID=$(curl -s -X POST https://api.autocontentapi.com/content/Create \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUTOCONTENT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"outputType": "audio",
       "resources": [{"type": "website",
                      "content": "https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/"}],
       "language": "English"}' | jq -r '.request_id // empty')

if [ -z "$REQUEST_ID" ]; then
  echo "Create failed" >&2
else
  # Ask every 30 seconds until "status" is 100 (done) or "error_code" is set.
  until curl -s https://api.autocontentapi.com/content/Status/$REQUEST_ID \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUTOCONTENT_API_KEY" > status.json &&
    jq -e '.status == 100 or .error_code > 0' status.json > /dev/null; do
    sleep 30
  done
  jq -r '.audio_url // .' status.json
fi
```

Last passed: November 2, 2026 (request 24587e3b-8d1e-47fb-96f0-d38e3b9f9770, result in 13.8 minutes).

Python 3 (pip install requests)

```
import os
import time

import requests

API = "https://api.autocontentapi.com"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['AUTOCONTENT_API_KEY']}"}

job = requests.post(
    f"{API}/content/Create",
    headers=HEADERS,
    json={
        "outputType": "audio",
        "resources": [{"type": "website", "content": "https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/"}],
        "language": "English",
    },
    timeout=60,
)
job.raise_for_status()
request_id = job.json()["request_id"]

while True:
    time.sleep(30)
    status = requests.get(f"{API}/content/Status/{request_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()
    if status["status"] == 100 or status.get("error_code"):
        break

print(status.get("audio_url") or status)
```

Last passed: November 2, 2026 (request ac040e13-1ae9-4540-8083-6695201e2ab2, result in 7.4 minutes).

Node.js 18+ (built-in fetch; save as podcast.mjs)

```
const API = 'https://api.autocontentapi.com';
const headers = {
  Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.AUTOCONTENT_API_KEY}`,
  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
};

const created = await fetch(`${API}/content/Create`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers,
  body: JSON.stringify({
    outputType: 'audio',
    resources: [{ type: 'website', content: 'https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/' }],
    language: 'English',
  }),
});
if (!created.ok) throw new Error(`Create failed: ${created.status} ${await created.text()}`);
const { request_id: requestId } = await created.json();

let status;
do {
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 30_000));
  status = await (await fetch(`${API}/content/Status/${requestId}`, { headers })).json();
} while (status.status !== 100 && !status.error_code);

console.log(status.audio_url || status);
```

## How AutoContent API makes these outputs

### How does it work?

Audio and video overviews, slide decks and infographics are made with Google's Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM), on accounts that AutoContent operates. Custom-script podcasts, transcripts, deep research, shorts, avatars and X posts are made only by our own pipeline on licensed APIs. AutoContent has no agreement with Google. Google can limit or stop this access at any time.

### Is that allowed by Google's terms?

We have no agreement with Google, and we can't give a legal opinion on Google's terms. The practical answer: Google can stop our access at any time, and that is the biggest risk of using us. If you need a contracted Google supply, use Google's Gemini Notebook Enterprise API.

### How do you run the accounts?

We don't share operational details.

## FAQ

### Does Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) have an API?

Yes, in a limited form. Google's Gemini Notebook API is a Public Preview for personal Google accounts that only creates notebooks and adds sources; it generates no content of any kind and cannot answer questions. Google also documents the Gemini Notebook Enterprise API: a Preview for Google Cloud projects with Enterprise licenses, which creates audio overviews. Google's Podcast API is deprecated and takes no new customers.

### Does the NotebookLM API charge for calls?

Google's Gemini Notebook API has no charge during its Public Preview. Google's Enterprise API docs show no price per call. You pay $9 per license per month, with at least 15 licenses, and each licensed user can make 20 audio overviews per day. AutoContent API, a separate service, charges 10 credits per finished podcast; status calls and failed generations use 0 credits.

### Is there a NotebookLM API key?

Not from Google. The Gemini Notebook API takes no API keys: it uses an OAuth 2.0 token of a personal Google account. Google's Enterprise API uses the Google Cloud sign-in of a licensed user, not a simple key. Third-party services issue their own keys; AutoContent API, a separate service, issues its own key with a paid plan.

### Can Google's Gemini Notebook API make audio overviews?

No. In the Public Preview it generates no content of any kind: no audio or video overviews, reports, mind maps, quizzes, infographics or slide decks, and no answers to questions. Its docs cover notebooks and sources only, and Google says that more is coming. For audio overviews under a Google contract, use the Enterprise API. For finished podcasts, videos, slide decks and infographics from one REST call, AutoContent API is an independent alternative.

### Is the Gemini Notebook Enterprise API free?

No. After a trial (30 days on Google's product page, 14 days in its licensing docs), it costs $9 per license per month, with at least 15 licenses: $135 per month or more.

### Can Google's Enterprise API make video overviews, slide decks or infographics?

No. Its docs cover notebooks, sources and audio overviews only. Video overviews, slide decks and infographics exist in the Enterprise app, not in the API.

### What happened to Google's Podcast API?

Google marks it deprecated and adds no new customers to its allowlist (page updated November 7, 2026). It makes a podcast of typically 4 to 5 minutes or around 10 minutes from text or media, with no notebook.

### Can I automate my own Gemini Notebook account?

Open-source tools such as notebooklm-py and gemini-notebook-mcp-cli drive your own account with cookies from your browser. Their own docs say they use undocumented endpoints, and they warn about rate limits, account restrictions and Google's terms. We describe them from their docs and do not run them.

### How long does a podcast take with AutoContent API?

In our test on November 2, 2026, 7.4 to 13.8 minutes from the request to the file. In the 30 days to November 2, 2026, the median was 11.5 minutes, and 95% finished within 90 minutes.

### Is AutoContent API affiliated with Google?

No. AutoContent API is an independent service. It is not affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by Google. Gemini, Gemini Notebook and NotebookLM are trademarks of Google LLC.

AutoContent API turns a URL, PDF, YouTube video or text into a finished podcast, video, slide deck or infographic through one REST API, with webhooks. Plans start at €29 per month.
